correctness.rationale: With fixed interior marginals the feasible table is P(z)=(z,r-z,c-z,1-r-c+z). The first-order equation equates its log odds Theta(z) to the checkerboard contrast h(X). Theta is strictly increasing onto R, with Theta'=H, so every interior z is realizable and the positive optimum is unique. The input contrast has max-entry dual norm 4 and the output checkerboard has max-entry norm 1. Integrating the derivative gives the global bound, and perturbing the realizing kernel at z_* in the checkerboard direction proves sharpness as a supremum. H'' is twice the sum of the four inverse cubes, and endpoint blow-up makes its minimizer unique. Row and column reciprocal-pair bounds are 4/[r(1-r)] and 4/[c(1-c)], respectively, with equality exactly for equal splits in the relevant pairs. If c=1/2 the row bound attains the smaller variance, and symmetrically if r=1/2. At independence, H'(rc) is minus (1-2r)(1-2c) divided by the positive product r²(1-r)²c²(1-c)²; strict monotonicity of H' gives the association sign. Cost scaling by 1/epsilon is exact. No evidence of finite-pair attainment is needed.
residual_risks: Interior two-state marginals and exact entropy minimization only; no claim for changing marginals or approximate scaling.
